pr_records.title: Fix LDA between-class scatter sample weights
pr_records.body:
### Description

`LinearDiscriminantAnalysis` counts `y == i + 1` while using the mean for class `i`. Each mean therefore receives the next class's sample count, and the final class contributes nothing to between-class scatter. This changes the learned eigenvalues and projection, including for equally sized classes.

Use the matching zero-based class count. Add regression coverage against an independently constructed generalized scatter problem and verify that renaming class labels preserves the fitted discriminants. Update the existing Iris eigenvalue fixture to include all three classes' scatter.

### Related issues or pull requests

Fixes #1300.

Related #277 changes loadings/decomposition and #478 sorts eigenvectors; these changes do not correct this count lookup. This submits the existing fork correction from [e6304e4](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/commit/e6304e468872652771e55115d34347b29dba141d), with expanded independent numerical and class-renaming regressions. The earlier fork work and this PR address the same improvement.

### Validation

- On unchanged base `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`, the 9 new cases produce **8 failures and 1 passing identity control**.
- With this correction, the complete feature-extraction test directory passes: **39 tests**. The numerical reference uses `scipy.linalg.eigh(B, W)` with independently accumulated per-class scatter, avoiding the implementation's inverse-product solver.
- The unequal-size reproduction changes eigenvalues from `[10.63705464, 1.95218225]` to the reference `[15.39053819, 1.23909435]`.
- Changed-file Flake8 and `git diff --check` pass.
- Linux, Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.3.5, SciPy 1.17.0, scikit-learn 1.8.0. The full repository suite was not run.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a note to `docs/sources/CHANGELOG.md`.
- [x] Added independent numerical and class-renaming regressions.
- [x] Ran the affected feature-extraction test directory; the template permits focused testing for small changes.
- [x] Checked changed-file style with Flake8.
- [ ] Modified the User Guide notebook: no API change; this corrects the existing LDA calculation.

### Current CI

Both GitHub unit-test jobs pass, including the latest scikit-learn job. The [formatting job](https://github.com/rasbt/mlxtend/actions/runs/43743012901/job/132900097703?pr=1301) fails during dependency installation, before the formatters run: its Python 3.15.2 environment attempts to build locked SciPy 1.16.3 and cannot find OpenBLAS. Changed-file Black, isort and Flake8 pass locally.

pr_records.title: Bump soupsieve from 2.8.4 to 4.0
pr_records.body:
Bumps [soupsieve](https://github.com/facelessuser/soupsieve) from 2.8.4 to 4.0.
Release notes

Sourced from soupsieve's releases.

4.0

  • BREAK: The contents of an HTML template are no longer treated as part of the document. Selectors do not descend into a template, and elements inside one can't see beyond it, which also applies to pseudo-classes such as :lang(), :disabled, and :default. select and filter will still reach the contents of a template when they are called on the template itself, for example soup.template.select('p'). See the FAQ for more information.
  • BREAK: The contents of an iframe are no longer treated as a separate document, as they are not one in a browser. Elements in an iframe are normal children, so :root does not match them, and :default, :indeterminate, :checked, :dir(), :lang(), and :read-write treat them like any other element. Recent versions of html.parser, lxml, and html5lib all escape the contents of an iframe like a browser does, so this mostly affects XHTML, Python versions that still don't escape such content in their specific html.parser, and elements added to an iframe by hand. :-soup-contains() now also includes the escaped text in an iframe. See the FAQ for more information.
  • NEW: Update :disabled and :enabled to treat option and optgroup elements inside a disabled select as disabled, following a recent HTML specification update.
  • FIX: Fix the subsequent-sibling combinator and :has(~ ...) never matching top level elements of a fragment that has no root element, unless caching was disabled.
  • FIX: :indeterminate now treats a radio button group without a form as extending across the whole document instead of the top level element that contains it, and it no longer ignores radio buttons at the top level.
  • FIX: Fix :default to treat a button with a missing or invalid type, and an input with type="image", as submit buttons.
  • FIX: Fix :in-range and :out-of-range raising TypeError when the document contains an input without a type attribute.
  • FIX: :read-write (and :read-only) now treat contenteditable="plaintext-only" elements as editing hosts and match the editable elements inside an editing host, following the nearest contenteditable state.
  • FIX: :read-write (and :read-only) now ignore contenteditable on non-HTML elements, such as an SVG foreignObject, as the attribute only applies to HTML elements. Such elements inherit the state of their parent.
  • FIX: :checked now only matches the last radio button with a checked attribute in a radio button group, as in a browser, where a group is the radio buttons with the same name and form, including the form attribute. :default still matches all of them, and the contents of a template are unaffected as they are not connected.
  • FIX: :dir() and :defined no longer affect the rest of the selector list they are in. Previously, a selector list that used either of them could not have its combinators cross an iframe, ignored the specified namespaces, and matched nothing in XML, not even the parts that didn't use them. They still do not match in XML, but :not(:dir(ltr)) and :not(:defined) now do.
  • FIX: :default and :indeterminate now honor the form attribute, which can associate a submit button or radio button with a form it is not in, or leave it without a form. It is ignored in a template, as in the HTML specification. Submit buttons outside of a form can now be its default button.
  • FIX: :default, :checked, and :indeterminate now handle a form inside a form like a browser. In HTML, a browser ignores the nested form and takes its end tag for that of the parent, which matters for parsers that keep the nested form, such as html.parser. In XHTML and in a template, nested forms are real forms.
  • FIX: :checked now matches the option that a browser would select. Without multiple, that is only the last option with a selected attribute in a select, and if there are none and the select shows a single option, the first option that is not disabled. :default still only considers the selected attribute.
  • FIX: Fix [attribute!=value] excluding values that only start with the specified value, and in XML documents, type values that contain a newline.
  • FIX: Match the values of every attribute that the HTML specification lists as ASCII case insensitive (rel, method, lang, dir, ...) without ASCII case sensitivity on HTML elements in HTML documents, not just type. Non-HTML elements are matched case sensitively.
  • FIX: :dir() now matches non-HTML elements, such as SVG and MathML, by the direction they inherit from their

pr_records.title: FIX: find_filegroups import, None extension, rstrip escape, ignore_invisible recursive (gh-1283)
pr_records.body:
## Summary

Fixes gh-1283: multiple issues in `mlxtend.file_io.find_filegroups` and `find_files`.

## Changes

### `find_filegroups.py`
- **Import fix**: Import `find_files` function instead of module (was `AttributeError: module has no attribute 'find_files'`).
- **None/empty extension handling**: Treat `None` or `""` in `extensions` list as "accept all extensions" for secondary scans (was dropping all files when extension was `None`).
- **`rstrip` regex escape**: Escape the `rstrip` suffix so it's treated literally, not as regex. This prevents `"$"` in filenames from being interpreted as an anchor, and multi-char suffixes like `"ue"` from being interpolated.

### `find_files.py`
- **`ignore_invisible` recursive**: In recursive mode, skip hidden directories (those starting with `.`) entirely, not just files inside them.

### Tests (`test_find_filegroups.py`)
Added 4 regression tests:
1. `test_find_filegroups_none_extension_accepts_all` — `extensions=[None]` accepts all extensions in secondary scan
2. `test_find_filegroups_preserves_literal_dollar_stem` — `$` in filename preserved (not regex anchor)
3. `test_find_filegroups_rstrip_is_literal` — `rstrip` suffix strips literal characters
4. `test_find_files_recursive_ignores_invisible` — recursive search honors `ignore_invisible` for hidden directories

## Testing
All tests pass locally (4 new + existing). Lint clean (flake8).

pr_records.title: Apply the reported L1 penalty during MLP training
pr_records.body:
### Description

`MultiLayerPerceptron._compute_cost` includes an L1 penalty, but the weight updates omit its derivative. Changing `l1` therefore changes the reported cost without changing the trained weights.

Add the existing penalty's subgradient to both weight matrices. The existing cost convention is `0.5 * l1 * sum(abs(weights))`, so the update uses the corresponding factor of 0.5 and a zero subgradient at zero weights. Biases remain unpenalized. Document this cost convention; the default `l1=0` path is unchanged.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`.

- Seven regression/control cases: **4 failed, 3 passed** on unchanged master; **7 passed** with the fix.
- Central finite differences of the existing reported cost independently check the observed one-step weight updates for two positive L1 strengths, with and without L2. Controls cover zero L1, zero-valued weights and unchanged biases.
- `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_mlp_l1_updates.py mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_multilayerperceptron.py -q`: **21 passed**.
- Changed-file Black, isort, Flake8 and `git diff --check` passed.

Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.3.5. Validation checks the training update against the existing objective; it is not a model-quality benchmark. The full repository suite was not run.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added gradient and control regression tests.
- [x] Documented the existing L1 cost convention.
- [x] Relevant tests and changed-file style checks pass.

pr_records.title: Apply MLP learning-rate decay once per epoch
pr_records.body:
### Description

`MultiLayerPerceptron` divides its current learning rate inside every minibatch. With nonzero `decrease_const`, this compounds the decay repeatedly within an epoch and across epochs, instead of using the documented `eta / (1 + epoch * decrease_const)` schedule.

Compute that rate once at the start of each epoch and share it across all minibatches. The existing epoch-cost history supplies the completed-epoch count, so continued fitting retains the schedule and parameter reinitialization restarts it.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`.

- Nine new regression/control cases: **7 failed, 2 passed** on unchanged master; **9 passed** with the fix.
- Training parameters and costs are compared with explicit constant-rate one-epoch updates for two decay strengths and three minibatch counts. Identical training rows isolate the schedule from shuffled minibatch ordering. Additional cases cover continuation, reinitialization and zero decay.
- The existing deterministic decay fixture's expected training accuracy changes from **0.98 to 1.0** because the corrected rates change its training trajectory; its exact assertion is updated. This is not a general model-quality benchmark.
- `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_mlp_learning_rate_schedule.py mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_multilayerperceptron.py -q`: **23 passed**.
- Changed-file Black, isort, Flake8 and `git diff --check` passed.

Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.3.5. The full repository suite was not run.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added explicit-schedule regression/control tests.
- [x] Documented minibatch and continuation schedule behavior.
- [x] Relevant tests and changed-file style checks pass.

pr_records.title: Preserve MLP momentum history when continuing training
pr_records.body:
### Description

Continuing a `MultiLayerPerceptron` fit with nonzero momentum raises `UnboundLocalError`: the previous-gradient arrays are local variables initialized only when `init_params=True`.

Store those four history arrays on the fitted model. Each update retains the history for the next fit or a serialized-model round trip; reinitializing the parameters resets it. The existing momentum update equation is unchanged.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`.

- Seven new regression/control cases: **4 failed, 3 passed** on unchanged master; **7 passed** with the fix.
- For two nonzero momentum values, continued fitting and a real pickle round trip match uninterrupted training in all weights, biases and epoch costs. Zero-momentum and parameter-reinitialization cases are controls.
- `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_mlp_momentum_continuation.py mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_multilayerperceptron.py -q`: **21 passed**.
- Changed-file Black, isort, Flake8 and `git diff --check` passed.

Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.3.5. Validation covers a fixed momentum configuration and checkpoints produced by the corrected model. Enabling momentum after a zero-momentum fit and migrating older pickles without this history are outside this change's validation. The full repository suite was not run.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added continuation, serialization and reset regression/control tests.
- [x] Documented momentum-history retention.
- [x] Relevant tests and changed-file style checks pass.

pr_records.title: Resolve class labels in probability-based counterfactuals
pr_records.body:
### Description

Probability-based `create_counterfactual` currently uses `y_desired` directly as an array index. Valid class labels such as 10 or 20 raise `IndexError`; a label of -1 silently selects the last probability column, which can optimize the opposite class.

Resolve the desired label through `model.classes_` once before optimization. Reject unknown labels with a clear `ValueError`. Estimators exposing only `predict_proba` retain the existing positional-column convention, and prediction mode is unchanged.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`.

- Ten new regression/control cases: **6 failed, 4 passed** before the change; **10 passed** afterward.
- Actual LogisticRegression models check that counterfactuals are invariant under numeric, signed and string class relabeling, and that the resulting prediction is the requested class.
- In the signed-label example, the old result was **+2.148633** for the wrong class instead of the reference **-1.800684**.
- Unknown-class and metadata-free estimator cases verify the error and positional-compatibility boundaries.
- `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest mlxtend/evaluate/tests/test_counterfactual_class_labels.py mlxtend/evaluate/tests/test_counterfactual.py -q`: **15 passed**.
- Changed-file Black, isort, Flake8 and `git diff --check` passed.

Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.3.5, SciPy 1.17.0, scikit-learn 1.8.0. The existing medium-lambda case still emits its optimization-evaluation-limit warning. The full repository suite was not run.

### Related issues or pull requests

The distance-scaling change in #1233 and the feature-freezing/optimizer options in #1148 address separate behavior. Their source diffs retain positional probability indexing; this change does not modify the distance objective or optimization method.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added native regression/control tests.
- [x] Documented class-label resolution and the positional fallback.
- [x] Relevant tests and changed-file style checks pass.

pr_records.title: Align prefit voting probabilities with classifier labels
pr_records.body:
### Description

When `fit_base_estimators=False`, `EnsembleVoteClassifier` averages probability columns by position. Prefit classifiers can have different class subsets or class orders, so equal-width arrays silently mix unrelated classes; differing widths raise a ragged-array error.

Align each prefit classifier's probability columns with the ensemble's labels using `classes_`. Classes missing from an individual classifier receive zero probability before the existing weighted average. The same alignment is used by soft `transform`; hard voting and the path that fits base estimators retain their behavior.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`.

- Eight new regression/control cases: **5 failed, 3 passed** before the change; **8 passed** afterward.
- Tests use fitted native GaussianNB models with overlapping and unequal class subsets, numeric and string labels, and a different learned class order. They check the explicit weighted probability reference, normalization, predicted labels, transform shape, and preservation of fitted parameters. Ordinary full-class ensembles and hard voting are controls.
- `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_prefit_vote_classes.py mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_ensemble_vote_classifier.py -q`: **24 passed**.
- Changed-file Black, isort, Flake8 and `git diff --check` passed.

Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.3.5, scikit-learn 1.8.0. The existing prefit test emits its expected use-clones warning. The full repository suite was not run.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added regression/control tests.
- [x] Documented prefit probability-column alignment.
- [x] Relevant tests and changed-file style checks pass.

pr_records.title: Preserve automatic class inference across refits and cloning
pr_records.body:
### Description

`SoftmaxRegression` and `MultiLayerPerceptron` overwrite the `n_classes=None` constructor parameter with the first dataset's inferred class count. Later calls to `fit` retain that old output width: adding a class raises `IndexError`, while fitting fewer classes leaves extra outputs. Cloning an already fitted model also carries the accidental fixed class count into the clone.

Keep the constructor parameter unchanged and infer the output width when initializing parameters. One-hot encoding uses the fitted output layer's actual width, so `init_params=False` continues training the existing model and explicit `n_classes` settings retain their behavior. No additional fitted-state field is introduced.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`.

- Ten new regression/control cases: **6 failed, 4 passed** on unchanged master; **10 passed** after the fix.
- Both estimators are checked for growing and shrinking class vocabularies, cloning after fitting, explicit class counts, and continued training. Refitted/cloned outputs and costs match a fresh estimator with the same seed; continued training matches an uninterrupted run.
- `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_inferred_class_count.py mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_softmax_regression.py mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_multilayerperceptron.py -q`: **37 passed**.
- Changed-file Black, isort, Flake8 and `git diff --check` passed.

Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.3.5, scikit-learn 1.8.0. The full repository suite was not run.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added regression/control tests for both affected estimators.
- [x] Documented when automatic class-count inference runs.
- [x] Relevant tests and changed-file style checks pass.

pr_records.title: Fit Adaline reliably with rank-deficient features
pr_records.body:
### Description

Adaline's default analytical fit explicitly inverts `Xb.T @ Xb`. Duplicate or constant features, or more features than observations, make that matrix singular and prevent fitting. Nearly collinear features can also produce inaccurate fitted values because forming the normal equations squares the design matrix's condition number.

Solve the augmented least-squares problem directly with `numpy.linalg.lstsq(..., rcond=None)`. Full-rank inputs retain their ordinary least-squares solution. Rank-deficient inputs receive the minimum-norm solution, including the intercept; this behavior is now documented. The iterative SGD path is unchanged.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`.

- Six new regression/control cases: **5 failed, 1 passed** before the change; **6 passed** afterward.
- Duplicate, constant, zero-valued and wide feature matrices previously raised `LinAlgError`. On the near-collinear example, the old fitted values differed from the independent reference by up to **1.081**.
- The independent reference uses SciPy's pivoted-QR `gelsy` solver. Tests check coefficients, fitted values, residual orthogonality, predictions and input preservation.
- `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_adaline_least_squares.py mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_adaline.py -q`: **18 passed**.
- Changed-file Black, isort, Flake8 and `git diff --check` passed.

Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.3.5, SciPy 1.17.0. The full repository suite and downstream model-quality benchmarks were not run.

### Related issues or pull requests

The historical stable-OLS change #575 introduced alternative solvers for `LinearRegression`. This change addresses `Adaline`, whose analytical path still performs the normal-equation inverse.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added regression/control tests.
- [x] Documented the analytical solver's rank-deficient behavior.
- [x] Relevant tests and changed-file style checks pass.

pr_records.title: Resample fit parameters with bootstrap training rows
pr_records.body:
### Description

Both `bootstrap_point632_score` and `bias_variance_decomp` resample training rows but pass the original fit parameters to each fitted model. A `sample_weight` vector therefore becomes detached from the observations it describes. Duplicated observations can receive different weights, silently changing the model and the reported estimate.

Resample fit parameters that have one entry per training observation using the same bootstrap indices as X and y. Reuse scikit-learn's existing fit-parameter indexing helper, including support for lists, pandas Series and Pipeline-prefixed parameter names. Scalars, `None` and parameters of other lengths pass through unchanged. Both public docstrings now describe this behavior.

A deterministic weighted-mean regression example in the new tests illustrates the effect:

| Estimate | Original result | Correct weighted bootstrap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First OOB replicate MSE | 54.163005 | 45.831706 |
| Bias-variance decomposition expected loss | 17.846246 | 15.136038 |
| Bias-variance decomposition variance | 3.472789 | 1.115966 |

These values are checked against weighted means computed directly from the sampled observation indices, independently of the estimator and mlxtend's implementation.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`.

- Twenty-two new regression/control cases: **18 failed, 4 passed** on unchanged master; **22 passed** with this fix.
- The cases cover OOB and .632 scoring, the full MSE bias-variance decomposition, NumPy/list/Series weights, non-default pandas indices, Pipeline parameter names, input preservation, estimator cloning, scalar weights, and non-sample fit parameters.

pr_records.title: Preserve statistic scale in permutation-test comparisons
pr_records.body:
### Description

`permutation_test` uses NumPy's default absolute tolerance when deciding which null statistics tie the observed statistic. Rescaling a statistic can therefore change a result even though it preserves every ordering:

```python
x, y = [1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]
stat = lambda a, b: abs(np.mean(a) - np.mean(b))
permutation_test(x, y, func=stat)                      # 0.1
permutation_test(x, y, func=lambda a, b: 1e-12*stat(a,b)) # previously 1.0
```

The paired exact result similarly changes from `0.25` to `1.0`. The default relative tolerance also merges distinct float64 statistics separated by `1e-7` around one.

Use a relative tie tolerance of 100 times the observed floating-point statistic dtype's machine epsilon, with zero absolute tolerance. Integer statistics use exact comparisons instead of floating-point coercion. This follows the roundoff approach described in [SciPy's permutation-test notes](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.permutation_test.html#notes). Sampling, seeds, exact enumeration and the randomized-test correction remain unchanged.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`.

- Thirteen new native regression/control cases: **8 failed, 5 passed** on unchanged master; **13 passed** with the fix.
- Exact results are checked against independent enumeration using integer sums. Cases cover paired/unpaired tests, scales `1e-12`, `1`, `1e12`, float32/float64 custom statistics, genuine floating-point ties, nearby distinct values, and integer statistics above `2**53`.
- `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest mlxtend/evaluate/tests/test_permutation_precision.py mlxtend/evaluate/tests/test_permutation.py -q`: **23 passed**.

pr_records.title: Return Q=0, p=1 from cochrans_q when there are no discordant predictions
pr_records.body:
### Description

`cochrans_q` divides by `k * sum(R_i) - sum(R_i^2)` summed over samples. When there are no discordant predictions across models (every model is right or wrong together on every sample, e.g. identical models), that denominator is 0 and the function emitted `RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in scalar divide` and returned `(nan, nan)`.

With zero discordance the data agree perfectly with the null hypothesis, so this returns `Q = 0.0`, `p = 1.0`. This matches what `mcnemar(..., corrected=False)` does for the no-discordant case.

Before: `cochrans_q(y, m, m, m)` -> `(nan, nan)` plus a RuntimeWarning.
After: `(0.0, 1.0)`, no warning.

Added `test_no_discordant_predictions`; `test_cochran_q.py` and `test_mcnemar_test.py` pass; flake8 clean on the touched file. AI assistance was used; I reproduced and checked the behavior locally.

pr_records.title: Fix constant-column indexing when standardizing selected NumPy columns
pr_records.body:
### Code of Conduct

The repository's Code of Conduct and contributor guide were reviewed.

### Description

`standardize` uses original input-column numbers to index the compact standard-deviation array for selected columns. A selected constant column can raise `IndexError`, or overwrite another column's statistic and produce NaNs and incorrect scaling.

```python
import numpy as np
from mlxtend.preprocessing import standardize

X = np.array([[1., 7., 2.], [2., 7., 4.], [3., 7., 6.]])
standardize(X, columns=[1])
# IndexError: index 1 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 1

standardize(X, columns=[1, 0], return_params=True)
# Previously: [[nan, -1.], [nan, 0.], [nan, 1.]], stds=[0., 1.]
```

Use the existing constant-column mask to update the corresponding statistic positions. Selecting `[1]` now gives zeros, and `[1, 0]` gives a zero constant column and a correctly standardized signal, with standard deviations `[1., 0.81649658]`. Keep the no-constant case as a no-op so read-only fitted statistics remain usable.

Add 17 regression/control cases covering selected/reordered NumPy columns, pandas integer/string column labels, returned means and standard deviations, input preservation, and read-only parameter controls. Clarify the order of returned statistics in the docstring and add a changelog entry.

### Related issues or pull requests

No issue is linked. This is separate from #1208 / #1211: that change preserves supplied fitted parameters during transform and explicitly leaves fitting-time indexing edge cases outside its scope. This PR fixes selection indexing and retains the existing behavior of supplied parameters.

### Validation

pr_records.title: Select the strongest chi-squared feature when OneR errors tie
pr_records.body:
## Problem

With `resolve_ties='chi-squared'`, OneR appends a p-value only after leaving the candidate loop. It therefore chooses the first tied feature regardless of association strength, and `p_value_` can describe a different feature. The selection also uses `argmax` although stronger evidence of association has a smaller p-value.

## Change

Record each tied feature's p-value and select its minimum. Cover both column orders, check that the recorded p-value belongs to the selected feature, and retain a control for `resolve_ties='first'`. Add a changelog entry.

## Validation

- The new tests report **2 failures and 1 passing control** on unchanged master.
- `python -m pytest mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_oner.py mlxtend/classifier/tests/test_oner_ties.py -q`: **6 passed**.

Tested with Python 3.12.14 and SciPy 1.17.0. The full repository suite was not run.

pr_records.title: Compute Cochran and F-test object counts without enumerating model combinations
pr_records.body:
## Problem

Cochran's Q and the multiple-model F-test enumerate all `2 ** num_models` correctness patterns to obtain the squared per-object totals. This becomes impractical as more models are compared, although only one count per object is needed.

## Change

Accumulate each object's number of correct predictions directly in the existing model loop, then sum the squared counts. This takes O(num_objects * num_models) work and O(num_objects) additional storage; the statistical formulas and public APIs stay the same. Add analytical 80-model cases, order-invariance cases and a changelog entry.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest mlxtend/evaluate/tests/test_cochran_q.py mlxtend/evaluate/tests/test_f_test.py mlxtend/evaluate/tests/test_many_model_comparisons.py -q`: **15 passed**.
- A deterministic 16-model, 50-object comparison gives identical statistics and p-values before and after. Local medians of three runs changed from 0.684 s to 0.000120 s for Cochran's Q and from 0.619 s to 0.000431 s for the F-test. These are measurements from this environment, not a general performance guarantee.
- Black, Flake8 on the affected Python files, and `git diff --check`: passed.

Tested with Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.3.5 and SciPy 1.17.0. The full repository suite was not run. The 80-model regressions were not run on the exponential implementation.

Paired permutation buffers are always float64, which rounds integer observations above `2**53`. This can change an exactly enumerable two-pair result from p=0.25 to p=0. Use the common input dtype for the paired buffers and preserve existing floating-point behavior.

pr_records.title: Bump filelock from 3.29.1 to 4.2.1
pr_records.body:
Bumps [filelock](https://github.com/tox-dev/py-filelock) from 3.29.1 to 4.2.1.
Release notes

Sourced from filelock's releases.

4.2.1

  • On a singleton wrapper, close> and close> end only the holds that tasks acquired through that wrapper. A reader that arrives during close() gets the closed error instead of joining the ending hold. After synchronous code closes or force-releases the shared lock, the wrappers refuse to admit readers into the ended hold, and close() on such a wrapper returns. Closing one wrapper no longer ends a task's nested hold taken through another wrapper on the same path. #832
  • ReadWriteLock locks again after a release() that an exception from a signal handler interrupted. The async read-write wrappers stop admitting readers into such a level. The async read-write locks forget a hold whose backend release failed after the backend let go, and they free the memory of each acquire that times out or is canceled. AsyncFileLock returns from release() after a few hundred acquires gave up behind a waiting one. An exception from a signal handler delivered while an AsyncFileLock call joins its queue no longer blocks every later call on that lock. #833
  • Fix ReadWriteLock acting on -journal, -wal or -shm files another process puts beside its database: a write could land in another file, a reader could get in beside a writer, and an acquire could fail. SQLite now opens the database by name only in a directory no other account can write, and through a private hard link elsewhere. On Windows the directory's access control list decides. Where hard links are unavailable, keep the database in a directory other accounts cannot write, such as one under %LOCALAPPDATA%. The lock removes link directories through a checked descriptor rather than by name, reads a link directory's name only when the locking account owns it, and leaves alone a directory with other content renamed onto a link directory's name. A database whose schema takes more than a few kilobytes to load raises ValueError instead of running past the acquire timeout. #834
  • Fix five bugs in opening the lock file. UnixFileLock no longer truncates a file it did not create, such as one renamed to the lock path, and no longer applies mode to it. An on_acquired hook that writes holder metadata now truncates the file itself. A lease (Linux) or an oplock (Windows) on the lock file or a soft lock's marker no longer holds acquire() past its timeout or blocking=False, and an oplock no longer holds release(); ReadWriteLock on Windows waits for its timeout and raises Timeout. On Windows, a mode without group and other bits, such as 0o600, now creates the lock file with an owner-only permission list; the ReadWriteLock database gets the same. The soft locks' writability check no longer follows a symlink swapped in at the lock path. On a filesystem without flock, a contender from another account now waits on a marker it cannot write instead of raising PermissionError. #835
  • Fix SoftFileLock, MarkerSoftFileLock and SoftFileLease removing a live holder's marker in three cases: the holder and the contender run in Linux time namespaces with different boottime offsets; only one of them can read the boot id; a process other than the owner rewrote the marker. Soft markers no longer carry group or other write bits. A process name containing a carriage return or another line separator no longer makes the stale check raise ValueError. When /proc/self/ns/time exists but cannot be read, the stale check no longer compares start times and keeps the marker. #836
  • The async read-write locks record their hold under a task owner, so synchronous code on the executor thread that took the hold can no longer re-enter or release it. AsyncSoftReadWriteLock gives back one level on release, so synchronous readers of a shared singleton keep theirs. SoftReadWriteLock tracks read levels per thread: release() from a thread that holds none raises RuntimeError. After its heartbeat recorded a lost hold, it refuses new acquires until that hold is released. #838
  • StrictSoftFileLock creates <path>.filelock and its claims directory with the lock's mode and sets the sticky bit (a directory flag that lets only a file's owner remove it) on both. On the next acquisition it narrows a directory it owns that an earlier release created wider; it leaves a directory of another account as it is, so remove such leftovers by hand. It reaches claims through a descriptor opened without following symlinks; on Windows it holds both directories open and refuses a junction (a directory that points at another directory). Under a sticky parent such as /tmp it refuses a coordination directory of another account, as SoftReadWriteLock does for <path>.rw. One read grace now covers a whole claim scan, a failed claim cleanup no longer leaves the sentinel descriptor open, and a non-regular node at a sentinel private-record name raises SoftFileLockProtocolError. On Windows, contenders read claims without blocking their owner's unlink. #839

... (truncated)

Sourced from filelock's changelog.

  • Handle EFTYPE when a no-follow open refuses a symlink in a soft reader/writer lock's protocol tree, so heartbeat reports lost ownership rather than a transient refresh error.

4.2.2 (2026-10-18)

  • Fix a lock on a relative path that stayed held after a later with lock: ended, when an earlier acquire() had failed because the working directory no longer exists. That call still raises :class:FileNotFoundError, and it now leaves the lock's hold count unchanged. :pr:856

4.2.1 (2026-10-17)

  • On a singleton wrapper, :meth:AsyncReadWriteLock.close() <filelock.AsyncReadWriteLock.close> and :meth:AsyncSoftReadWriteLock.close() <filelock.AsyncSoftReadWriteLock.close> end only the holds that tasks acquired through that wrapper. A reader that arrives during close() gets the closed error instead of joining the ending hold. After synchronous code closes or force-releases the shared lock, the wrappers refuse to admit readers into the ended hold, and close() on such a wrapper returns. Closing one wrapper no longer ends a task's nested hold taken through another wrapper on the same path. :pr:832
  • :class:~filelock.ReadWriteLock locks again after a release() that an exception from a signal handler interrupted. The async read-write wrappers stop admitting readers into such a level. The async read-write locks forget a hold whose backend release failed after the backend let go, and they free the memory of each acquire that times out or is canceled. :class:~filelock.AsyncFileLock returns from release() after a few hundred acquires gave up behind a waiting one. An exception from a signal handler delivered while an :class:~filelock.AsyncFileLock call joins its queue no longer blocks every later call on that lock. :pr:833
  • Fix :class:~filelock.ReadWriteLock acting on -journal, -wal or -shm files another process puts beside its database: a write could land in another file, a reader could get in beside a writer, and an acquire could fail. pr_records.title: Feature/calibration metrics
pr_records.body:
### Code of Conduct

I have read and agree to the [Code of Conduct](https://rasbt.github.io/mlxtend/Code-of-Conduct/).

### Description

Adds calibration metrics to `mlxtend.evaluate` for checking whether a
classifier's predicted probabilities can be trusted (e.g. whether predictions
made with 90% confidence are actually correct ~90% of the time).

New functions:
- `expected_calibration_error(y_target, y_proba, n_bins=10, strategy="uniform")`:
  sample-weighted average of |accuracy − confidence| across confidence bins (ECE)
- `maximum_calibration_error(...)`: worst-case bin gap (MCE)
- `reliability_table(...)`: per-bin count, mean confidence, accuracy and gap,
  i.e. the data behind a reliability diagram

Features:
- Binary input as 1D P(class 1) or 2D `predict_proba` output, and multiclass input
- `"uniform"` (equal-width) or `"quantile"` (equal-count) binning
- Input validation with clear error messages (shape mismatch, values outside
  [0, 1], NaN, rows not summing to 1, invalid labels, invalid `n_bins`/`strategy`)

Files changed:
- `mlxtend/evaluate/calibration.py` – new module with NumPy-style docstrings and doctest examples
- `mlxtend/evaluate/__init__.py` – exports the three new functions
- `mlxtend/evaluate/tests/test_calibration.py` – 18 unit tests
- `examples/calibration_example.py` – compares Logistic Regression, Gaussian NB
  and Random Forest on the breast cancer dataset

pr_records.title: Add corrected resampled paired t test (#376)
pr_records.body:
### Code of Conduct

I have read and agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://rasbt.github.io/mlxtend/Code-of-Conduct/).

### Description

Adds `mlxtend.evaluate.paired_ttest_corrected_resampled`, the corrected resampled paired *t* test by Nadeau and Bengio (2003), as requested in #376.

`paired_ttest_resampled` treats the score differences from overlapping train/test splits as independent, which underestimates their variance and leads to too many false positives. The corrected test replaces the variance factor `1/J` with `1/J + n_test/n_train`, where `J` is the number of splits. Used with repeated *k*-fold splits, this is the corrected repeated *k*-fold cv test by Bouckaert and Frank (2004).

**API.** Same parameters, defaults and return values as `paired_ttest_resampled`, plus an optional `cv`:

```python
from mlxtend.evaluate import paired_ttest_corrected_resampled

t, p = paired_ttest_corrected_resampled(
    estimator1, estimator2, X, y,
    num_rounds=30, test_size=0.3,  # same defaults as paired_ttest_resampled
    cv=None,                       # or any sklearn splitter, e.g. RepeatedStratifiedKFold
    scoring=None, random_seed=None,
)
```

- Without `cv`, it generates exactly the same splits as `paired_ttest_resampled` for the same `random_seed`, so the only difference between the two results is the correction (a unit test checks this).
- Estimators are cloned and refit on the training part of every split, so the estimators passed in stay unfitted and test data is never used for fitting. The user guide recommends putting preprocessing inside a `Pipeline`.
- Works with NumPy arrays, pandas DataFrames, SciPy sparse matrices and Python lists.
- Inputs are validated with clear error messages. If every split gives the same score difference, it returns `(0.0, 1.0)` for a zero difference and `(±inf, 0.0)` otherwise, instead of dividing by zero.

**Example** (iris, logistic regression vs. decision tree, same 30 splits):

| | t | p |
|---|---|---|
| `paired_ttest_resampled` | 3.616 | 0.001 |
| `paired_ttest_corrected_resampled` | 0.971 | 0.339 |

**Simulation.** I also checked the behavior on 1000 synthetic datasets where both models are equally good by construction (two logistic-regression pipelines, each using one of two equally informative features). At α = 0.05, the uncorrected resampled test rejected in 56.5% of the datasets; the corrected test rejected in 4.6%, and the corrected 10x10 repeated stratified *k*-fold variant in 4.5%. When one model was truly better by about 5 accuracy points or more, the corrected test rejected significantly more often than `combined_ftest_5x2cv` (paired over the same datasets, also after adjusting for the tests' different false positive rates). The simulation code is not part of this PR; I'm happy to share it.

**Changes**

- `mlxtend/evaluate/ttest.py`: new function
- `mlxtend/evaluate/__init__.py`: export
- `mlxtend/evaluate/tests/test_paired_ttest_corrected_resampled.py`: 17 tests (formula against hand-computed values, consistency with `paired_ttest_resampled`, classifier and regressor defaults, scoring strings and callables, `RepeatedStratifiedKFold` and `StratifiedShuffleSplit`, seeds including 0, return types, no side effects, pipelines with `ColumnSelector`, pandas, sparse and list input, zero-variance cases, invalid inputs)
- `docs/sources/user_guide/evaluate/paired_ttest_corrected_resampled.ipynb`: new user-guide page; added to `docs/mkdocs.yml` and both user-guide indexes
- `docs/sources/user_guide/evaluate/paired_ttest_resampled.ipynb`: one sentence pointing to the corrected test
- `docs/sources/CHANGELOG.md`: entry under New Features and Enhancements

If you'd prefer a `corrected=True` option on `paired_ttest_resampled` instead of a separate function, I'm happy to change it.

pr_records.title: Honor random_seed=0 in shuffle_arrays_unison (#1239)
pr_records.body:
### Description

`shuffle_arrays_unison` checked the seed with `if random_seed:`, which treats `0` as false. As a result, `random_seed=0` was silently ignored and the shuffle depended on NumPy's global random state. The check is now `if random_seed is not None:`, so zero seeds the generator like any other integer, and `None` keeps its existing behavior.

`shuffled_split` calls `shuffle_arrays_unison` internally, so `shuffled_split(..., random_seed=0)` had the same bug and is fixed by the same change.

**Changes**

- `mlxtend/preprocessing/shuffle.py`: the one-line guard fix, and a clearer `random_seed` docstring for both functions (any integer including 0 is reproducible; `None` uses the global random state).
- `mlxtend/preprocessing/tests/test_shuffle_shuffle_arrays_unison.py`: new tests for
  - `random_seed=0` (the regression from #1239), for both `shuffle_arrays_unison` and `shuffled_split`
  - positive seeds being reproducible regardless of the global random state
  - `random_seed=None` still drawing from the global random state (unchanged behavior)
  - rows staying aligned across the shuffled arrays

  The existing test compared `X2.all() == expected.all()`, which compares two booleans and could not fail. It now uses `np.testing.assert_array_equal` with the same expected values.
- `docs/sources/CHANGELOG.md`: entry under 0.26.0.

**Verification:** with the old guard, the two zero-seed tests fail and the other four pass; with the fix, all six pass. `pytest mlxtend/preprocessing` passes (49 tests), and flake8, black and isort report no issues.

pr_records.body:
Bumps [urllib3](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3) from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0.
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.8.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

Deprecations & Removals

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

Features

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)

  • Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)

  • Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)

  • Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)

  • Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)

  • Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)

  • Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)

  • Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)

  • Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)

  • Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

  • Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

pr_records.title: Fix/counterfactual distance stability
pr_records.body:
### Code of Conduct

I have reviewed the project's Code of Conduct and contribution guidelines.

### Description

This pull request improves numerical stability in MLxtend's `create_counterfactual()` function.

Previously, the distance calculation used the absolute difference between each feature's dataset median and the reference instance. When this difference was zero, the calculation could produce `NaN` or infinite values, affecting counterfactual optimization.

This contribution:

- Replaces the previous distance scaling with feature-wise median absolute deviation (MAD).
- Uses a unit-scale fallback for features with zero MAD to avoid division by zero.
- Preserves the existing public function API.
- Adds regression tests covering constant features, zero-MAD cases, deterministic behavior, and existing prediction and probability modes.
- Updates the function documentation, user guide, and changelog.

The change is intended to improve the reliability of counterfactual explanations, particularly when datasets contain constant or low-variation features.

**Compatibility note:** The public API remains unchanged, but counterfactual values may differ because the distance metric has been corrected.

### Related issues or pull requests

Related: #1029 and #1148.

This contribution addresses distance scaling and numerical stability. It does not implement the `fixed_features` functionality proposed in PR #1148.

pr_records.title: Fix feature_importance_permutation permuting the wrong columns for feature_groups
pr_records.body:
### Code of Conduct

I have read the code of conduct.

### Description

With `feature_groups`, `feature_importance_permutation` shuffled `X[:, i]` for `i in range(len(group))`, i.e. the *first* columns of `X`, whenever a group was given as a list or range. The extra `rng.shuffle(X[:, feat])` only shuffled a fancy-indexed copy. So `[[2], [3]]` both permuted column 0, and the one-hot group `range(3, 21)` from the user guide permuted columns 0–17.

Each group is now permuted by applying one row permutation to all of its columns:

```python
X[:, feat] = save_col[rng.permutation(X.shape[0])]
```

This affects only the group's columns, keeps one-hot rows valid, and works the same for integer, list and range groups. For integer groups `rng.permutation(n)` gives the same ordering as the previous `rng.shuffle(X[:, feat])`, so those results don't change for a given seed.

pr_records.body:
### Code of Conduct

I have read the code of conduct.

### Description

`vectorspace_dimensionality` sums the norms of the orthonormalized columns and converts that sum with `int(...)`, which truncates. After normalization a column norm can be `0.9999999999999999`, so for example `np.array([[1, 0], [2, 0]])` returned 0 instead of 1. This PR rounds the sum before the conversion. The columns are either unit vectors or exactly zero, so the sum is always within floating-point error of the true dimensionality.

pr_records.title: Fix RecursionError in num_combinations, num_permutations and factorial
pr_records.body:
### Code of Conduct

I have read the code of conduct.

### Description

`factorial` in `mlxtend.math` was recursive, so `factorial`, `num_combinations` and `num_permutations` raised `RecursionError`:

- for large `n` past the recursion limit, e.g. `num_combinations(1200, 2)`;
- for `k > n` without replacement, where `factorial(n - k)` got a negative argument and never reached the base case.

This PR switches the three functions to the standard library's `math.factorial`, `math.comb` and `math.perm`. These are exact integer implementations, so results for valid inputs don't change. pr_records.title: Clip the relative overfitting rate in the .632+ bootstrap
pr_records.body:
### Code of Conduct

I have read the code of conduct.

### Description

`bootstrap_point632_score(..., method=".632+")` computes the weight `0.632 / (1 - 0.368 * R)` from the relative overfitting rate `R = (test_err - train_err) / (gamma - train_err)`, but `R` was not clipped. Efron and Tibshirani (1997, Eq. 32) set `R` to 0 unless the out-of-bag error is larger than the training error (and gamma is larger than the training error), and cap the out-of-bag error at the no-information error rate `gamma`, so `R` stays in [0, 1] and the weight in [0.632, 1].

Without the clipping, the weight can be negative or larger than 1:

```python
import numpy as np
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
from mlxtend.evaluate import bootstrap_point632_score

rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
X, y = rng.randn(40, 2), rng.randint(0, 2, 40)  # random labels
scores = bootstrap_point632_score(DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=0), X, y,
                                  method=".632+", random_seed=1)
scores.min()  # before: -0.648 (a negative accuracy), after: 0.369
```

A constant model such as `DummyClassifier(strategy="most_frequent")` has a training error equal to `gamma`, so the old code divided by zero (RuntimeWarning). It now gets `R = 0`, and `.632+` reduces to `.632`, as in the paper.

The clipping is written in terms of `R` only, so it behaves the same for accuracy-type scores and for loss functions like the default MSE for regressors. When `0 <= R <= 1`, the result is unchanged. In the existing test, the full decision tree result (0.95855) stays the same. The depth-1 tree changes slightly (0.64078 -> 0.6409) because some rounds had `R < 0`.

I also added one sentence about the clipping to the .632+ section of the user guide.

pr_records.title: Return a two-sided p-value from proportion_difference
pr_records.body:
### Code of Conduct

I have read the code of conduct.

### Description

`proportion_difference` computed the p-value as `scipy.stats.norm.cdf(z)`, which is the lower-tail probability. As a result, the p-value depended on the order of the two proportions, and two equal proportions got p = 0.5:

```python
from mlxtend.evaluate import proportion_difference
proportion_difference(0.84, 0.92, n_1=100)  # z = -1.754, p = 0.040
proportion_difference(0.92, 0.84, n_1=100)  # z =  1.754, p = 0.960
proportion_difference(0.92, 0.92, n_1=100)  # z =  0.0,   p = 0.5
```

The null hypothesis of the test is that the two proportions are equal, and the user guide uses the two-sided critical value 1.96. So this PR returns the two-sided p-value `2 * norm.sf(|z|)`. It is now 0.079 for both orderings above and 1.0 for equal proportions. This also matches the other tests in `mlxtend.evaluate`, such as the paired t-tests and `mcnemar`.

In the user guide example the p-value changes from 0.040 to 0.079. I updated the stored output and the sentence after it, which said the difference was significant.

### Code of Conduct

I have read the code of conduct.

### Description

`TransactionEncoder.transform(X, sparse=True)` built the CSR matrix without a `shape`. scipy therefore inferred the number of columns from the largest column index present in `X`, which caused two problems:

```python
te = TransactionEncoder().fit([["a", "b", "c"]])
te.transform([["a"]], sparse=True).shape

```

When the two models never disagree (b + c == 0), `mcnemar()` divided by zero.
```python
>>> mcnemar(np.array([[8, 0], [0, 2]]))
(inf, 0.0)    # before (plus a RuntimeWarning)
(0.0, 1.0)    # after
```

pr_records.title: Document public parameters that are missing from the docstrings
pr_records.body:
Four public functions take a parameter that their `Parameters` section never mentions, so the parameter does not appear in the rendered API docs at all.

### `category_scatter` — `label_col`

```python
def category_scatter(x, y, label_col, data, markers="sxo^v", ...):
```

`label_col` is the third positional argument and the reason the function exists — one scatter series is drawn per unique value in that column — but the docstring goes straight from `y` to `data`. The new entry follows the wording already used for `x` and `y`, since `label_col` takes a column name for a `DataFrame` and a column index for an `ndarray` (asserted at the top of the body).

### `apriori` — `n_jobs`

Selects the number of `joblib.Parallel` workers. It is worth being specific about when it applies: the `low_memory=True` branch and the sparse-input branch never reference `n_jobs`, so it only affects the default dense path. The entry says so rather than implying the whole function is parallelized.

### `association_rules` — `return_metrics`

Chooses which metric columns are computed and included in the result. The default is the full `_metrics` list, which the entry spells out.

### `plot_learning_curves` — malformed entry name

```
    suppress_plot=False : bool (default: False)
```

The name field contains `=False`, so numpydoc parses the parameter name as `suppress_plot=False`. Every other entry in the same docstring uses `name : type (default: X)`; this one just needs the default dropped from the name field, where it is already repeated on the right.

---

Two parameters were deliberately left alone:

- `PCA.fit(X, y)` — `y` is the ignored scikit-learn compatibility argument, and no sibling `fit` in `feature_extraction` documents it either.

pr_records.title: Fix plotting docstrings that name parameters the functions do not have
pr_records.body:
Two plotting docstrings name parameters that don't exist, so following them raises `TypeError`. Docs only, no behaviour change.

### `heatmap` documents `conf_mat`, parameter is `matrix`

```python
def heatmap(
    matrix,
    hide_spines=False,
    ...
```

```
    Parameters
    -----------
    conf_mat : array-like, shape = [n_rows, n_columns]
        And arbitrary 2D array.
```

`conf_mat` is the parameter name used by `plot_confusion_matrix`, so this looks like the docstring was adapted from that function and the name wasn't updated — the description right below it ("And arbitrary 2D array") reads like it was rewritten for the general case while the name stayed behind. Every other entry in the docstring matches the signature. I also corrected "And arbitrary" to "An arbitrary" on that same line.

### `scatterplotmatrix` documents `fix_axes`, parameter is `fig_axes`

```python
def scatterplotmatrix(
    X, fig_axes=None, names=None, figsize=(8, 8), alpha=1.0, **kwargs
):
```

The docstring says `fix_axes` in both the Parameters and the Returns sections, but it's inconsistent with itself — the `figsize` entry a few lines further down already refers to `fig_axes` correctly:

```
    figsize : tuple (default: (8, 8))
      Height and width of the subplot grid. Ignored if
      fig_axes is not `None`.
```

so `fix_axes` is a typo for `fig_axes` rather than a rename. Fixed both occurrences.

Both functions are public and have user-guide pages, so these are what the rendered API docs show.

Checked with `black --check` — both files unchanged.

pr_records.title: Correct documented default values that disagree with the signatures
pr_records.body:
### Code of Conduct

Read and agreed.

### Description

Eight parameter defaults are documented with a value the signature does not use:

| function | parameter | documented | actual |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lift_score` | `positive_label` | `0` | `1` |
| `paired_ttest_kfold_cv` | `shuffle` | `True` | `False` |
| `find_filegroups` | `validity_check` | `None` | `True` |
| `fpmax` | `null_values` | `True` | `False` |
| `plot_confusion_matrix` | `figsize` | `(2.5, 2.5)` | `None` |
| `plot_confusion_matrix` | `norm_colormap` | `False` | `None` |
| `heatmap` | `figsize` | `(2.5, 2.5)` | `None` |
| `checkerboard_plot` | `figsize` | `(2.5, 2.5)` | `None` |

The first four affect results rather than appearance:

- `positive_label` selects which class the lift is computed for, so a reader who trusts the docstring expects the score for class `0`.
- `shuffle` changes the CV split the paired t-test runs on.
- `validity_check` gates a check that raises (`if validity_check:` in `find_filegroups`).
- `null_values` is threaded through `valid_input_check`, `setup_fptree` and the generator.

For `figsize`, neither `plot_confusion_matrix` nor `heatmap` actually falls back to `(2.5, 2.5)` — both scale with the matrix:

```python
if figsize is None:
    figsize = (len(conf_mat) * 1.25, len(conf_mat) * 1.25)
```

and `checkerboard_plot` passes `None` straight through to matplotlib, so the effective size is matplotlib's own default rather than `(2.5, 2.5)`. `norm_colormap` reaches `ax.matshow(norm=...)`, which expects a `Normalize` instance or `None`, not a bool.

Only docstrings are changed — no behaviour is touched. I checked the rest of the package for the same problem; the other near-matches (`find_filegroups.substring`, `scatterplotmatrix.figsize`, `scatter_hist.figsize`, `standardize.params`, `plot_decision_regions.feature_index`) are all correct as written and are left alone.

### Related issues or pull requests

None.

- [ ] Added appropriate unit test functions in the `./mlxtend/*/tests` directories (if applicable) — not applicable, docstring-only

pr_records.title: apriori: make low_memory match the default result at exact support boundaries
pr_records.body:
`apriori(..., low_memory=True)` can silently drop an itemset whose support lands exactly on `min_support`, while the default path keeps it. The two paths are documented as producing the same result (`low_memory` is described only as a slower, memory-efficient mode).

The default path compares the normalized support: `count / rows_count >= min_support`. The `low_memory` path instead scaled the threshold (`threshold = min_support * rows_count`) and compared raw counts against it. That multiplication can round up: for 25 rows and `min_support=0.28`, `0.28 * 25 == 7.000000000000001`, so an itemset with a count of exactly 7 (support `7/25 = 0.28`) fails `7 >= 7.000000000000001` and is dropped.

Repro:

```python
import pandas as pd
from mlxtend.frequent_patterns import apriori
from mlxtend.preprocessing import TransactionEncoder

tx = [['A', 'B']] * 7 + [['C']] * 18   # {A, B} support = 7/25 = 0.28
te = TransactionEncoder()
df = pd.DataFrame(te.fit(tx).transform(tx), columns=te.columns_)

apriori(df, min_support=0.28)                    # includes {A, B}
apriori(df, min_support=0.28, low_memory=True)   # drops {A, B}
```

The fix compares the normalized support directly (`supports / rows_count >= min_support`), matching the default path's arithmetic so the two modes agree. The yielded support values are unchanged. Added a regression test at the exact boundary; the existing `test_low_memory_matches_default_result` uses data that does not land on a float boundary, so it did not catch this.

Changelog

Sourced from cryptography's changelog.

50.0.0 - 2026-07-31


* **SECURITY ISSUE**:
  :func:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization.pkcs7.pkcs7_decrypt_der`
  and its PEM and S/MIME variants no longer expose distinguishable errors or
  timing when unwrapping a ``RecipientInfo``'s ``encryptedKey``, which could
  act as a Bleichenbacher oracle for callers that decrypt untrusted messages.
  A random key is now substituted on failure, as described in :rfc:`3218`.
  Credit to **@X1AOxiang** for reporting the issue. **CVE-2026-69247**
* Deprecated Diffie-Hellman key exchange over finite fields (FFDH).
  Everything FFDH is deprecated, including the types in
  ``cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.dh`` and loading FFDH keys or
  parameters with the key loading APIs. Users should migrate to a more
  modern key exchange algorithm.
* Added ``xof()`` class methods to
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.SHAKE128` and
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.SHAKE256` for constructing
  algorithm instances configured for use with
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.XOFHash`.
* The :mod:`X.509 verification <cryptography.x509.verification>` APIs are now
  considered stable and are subject to our API stability policy.
* Added the :doc:`/cobblestone` recipe, an implementation of the
  Cobblestone-128 and Cobblestone-256 instantiations of the `C2SP
  chunked-encryption specification
  <https://c2sp.org/chunked-encryption>`_ for streaming authenticated
  encryption of large messages.
* Parsing a Signed Certificate Timestamp list now rejects encodings that
  carry trailing bytes after the list or after an individual SCT, instead of
  silently ignoring them.
* Added support for using :class:`~cryptography.x509.Name` as a field type in
  the :doc:`/hazmat/asn1/index` module.
* Loading a public key or an EC private key now rejects DER where the
  ``subjectPublicKey`` (or EC ``publicKey``) ``BIT STRING`` declares a non-zero
  number of unused bits, instead of silently ignoring it.
* Parsing a CRL entry's ``InvalidityDate`` extension now rejects a
  ``GeneralizedTime`` that carries fractional seconds or another non-DER form,
  matching the strict encoding already required for every other X.509 time
  field.
* :func:`~cryptography.x509.ocsp.load_der_ocsp_request` and
  :func:`~cryptography.x509.ocsp.load_der_ocsp_response` now reject a request
  or response whose ``version`` field is not ``v1``, the only version defined
  by RFC 6960, matching the version validation already performed when loading
  certificates, CSRs and CRLs.
* :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.XOFHash` is now supported
  when building against AWS-LC.
* HMAC (and therefore PBKDF2-HMAC) with SHA-3 hashes is now supported when
  building against AWS-LC.
* Diffie-Hellman (:doc:`/hazmat/primitives/asymmetric/dh`) is now supported
  when building against AWS-LC.

pr_records.title: Add mutual information metric to association_rules
pr_records.body:
Adds a `mutual_information` metric to `association_rules()`, computed as the log2 of the lift, i.e. the pointwise mutual information between antecedent and consequent. This addresses issue #1114; the metric is also usable as a `metric=` filter and is added to the default returned columns alongside `kulczynski`.

Rebased onto current `master` — the previous version of this branch was failing the unit-test workflow because the metric values in the expected test fixtures no longer matched after upstream changes to the support/lift computation.

pr_records.title: fix: raise ValueError in minmax_scaling for constant columns
pr_records.body:
## Summary
Fixes the silent NaN bug in `minmax_scaling()` when a constant 
column (zero range) is passed.

## Problem
When all values in a column are identical:
- denominator = max - min = 0
- result = 0/0 = NaN (silent, only a RuntimeWarning is emitted)
- This can corrupt ML pipelines without any clear indication

## Fix
Added a zero-range check before the division:

```python
are_constant = denominator == 0
if np.any(are_constant):
    raise ValueError(
        "One or more columns have zero range (all values are identical). "
        "minmax_scaling cannot be applied to constant columns."
    )
```

## Why ValueError over silent 0.0
- Silent behavior hides data issues from the user
- Explicit errors are safer and easier to debug in ML pipelines
- Consistent with how standard libraries handle invalid input

## Testing
```python
import numpy as np
from mlxtend.preprocessing import minmax_scaling

# Constant column → raises ValueError
ary = np.array([[5,1],[5,2],[5,3]])
minmax_scaling(ary, columns=[0,1])  # ValueError ✅

# Normal case → still works
ary2 = np.array([[1,1],[2,2],[3,3]])
minmax_scaling(ary2, columns=[0,1])  # [[0. 0.][0.5 0.5][1. 1.]] ✅
```

Closes #1167

pr_records.title: evaluate: clarify avg_bias is squared bias in bias_variance_decomp (#1083)
pr_records.body:
## Summary

The `bias_variance_decomp` docstring describes the second return value as "average bias", but for the `mse` loss the function actually computes the average **squared** bias — `mean((main_predictions - y_test) ** 2)` — which is the `Bias^2` term in the standard `Loss = Bias^2 + Variance` decomposition. This mismatch is exactly the point raised in #1083, which the maintainer agreed should be clarified in the docs.

This PR is docstring-only (plus one inline code comment); no runtime behaviour changes. The variable name `avg_bias` is kept for backwards compatibility.

Fixes rasbt/mlxtend#1083 — *"Bias squared" rather than "Bias"?*

## Context

Two small problems in the current `Returns` section of `bias_variance_decomp`:

1. The text reads `"the average expected average bias, and average bias (all floats)"` — a copy-paste typo where `average variance` is duplicated as `average bias`.
2. There is no hint that, for the `mse` loss, `avg_bias` is the squared bias rather than the raw bias. Readers who match it against `Loss = Bias^2 + Variance` (as the original reporter did) expect a square root or an explicit note.

The maintainer confirmed in [#1083](https://github.com/rasbt/mlxtend/issues/1083#issuecomment-1825036569): *"Yes, that's a good point. It's average biased squared. Maybe it should be made more explicit in the docs like you suggest."*

## Changes

- `mlxtend/evaluate/bias_variance_decomp.py` — rewrote the `Returns` block to spell out the three values, fix the duplicated-variance typo, and add an explicit note about `avg_bias` being squared bias for `mse` (and the misclassification rate of the main prediction for `0-1_loss`). Also added a 4-line code comment next to the `mse` `avg_bias` computation so a reviewer reading the diff cold doesn't have to re-derive the invariant.
- `docs/sources/CHANGELOG.md` — one entry under "Version 0.25.0 (TBD)".

## Reproduce BEFORE/AFTER yourself (copy-paste)

```bash
# Expected: the Returns section reads

#    average bias, and average bias (all floats), where the average is
#    computed over the data points in the test set."
# i.e. "average bias" is duplicated and there is no Bias^2 vs Bias note.

# --- AFTER (this PR) ---

python -c "from mlxtend.evaluate import bias_variance_decomp; help(bias_variance_decomp)" | sed -n '/Returns/,/Examples/p'
# Expected: the Returns section now lists "average expected loss, average

```

The five non-Keras tests all pass.

pr_records.title: preprocessing: handle constant columns in minmax_scaling (#1167)
pr_records.body:
## Summary

`mlxtend.preprocessing.minmax_scaling` silently returns `NaN` for any column whose values are all identical: the per-column `denominator = max - min` is `0`, so `numerator / denominator` becomes `0 / 0` and numpy only emits a low-level `RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in divide`. The sibling function `standardize` in the same module already collapses constant columns to `0.0` (and documents it). This PR aligns `minmax_scaling` with that contract.

Fixes rasbt/mlxtend#1167 — *minmax_scaling returns NaN silently for constant columns*

## Context

The bug was reported on 2026-05-21 and points out the asymmetry with `standardize`: constant columns get NaN with no error path other than the numpy warning, which is easy to miss in a larger pipeline. The reporter's expected output (constant column at `0.0`, other columns scaled normally) matches what `standardize` already does, so the fix here is to make the two functions agree.

## Changes

- `mlxtend/preprocessing/scaling.py` — in `minmax_scaling`, replace any zero entry in `denominator` with `1` before the divide. The numerator for those columns is identically zero, so the column collapses to `0.0` (i.e. `min_val`) instead of `NaN`. Behaviour for non-constant columns is unchanged. The `Notes` section of the docstring now records the contract explicitly. The substitution uses `np.where(denominator == 0, 1, denominator)` — a 1-line guard with a 5-line comment explaining the invariant so a reviewer reading the diff cold doesn't have to re-derive it.
- `mlxtend/preprocessing/tests/test__scaling__minmax_scaling.py` — three new regression tests: numpy path with default `(0, 1)` range, pandas DataFrame path, and custom `(50, 100)` range. All three fail on `origin/master` and pass on this branch.
- `docs/sources/CHANGELOG.md` — one entry under "Version 0.25.0 (TBD)".

## Reproduce BEFORE/AFTER yourself (copy-paste)

```bash
# --- one-time setup ---
git clone https://github.com/rasbt/mlxtend.git /tmp/repro-1167 && cd /tmp/repro-1167
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e . pytest pytest-timeout

cat > /tmp/repro_1167.py <<'PY'
import numpy as np
from mlxtend.preprocessing import minmax_scaling

ary = np.array([[5, 1], [5, 2], [5, 3]])
out = minmax_scaling(ary, columns=[0, 1])
print(out)
print("has_nan =", bool(np.isnan(out).any()))
PY

# --- BEFORE (origin/master) ---
git checkout origin/master
pip install -e . --quiet
python /tmp/repro_1167.py
# Expected: column 0 is [nan, nan, nan], "has_nan = True", and a RuntimeWarning

# --- AFTER (this PR) ---
git fetch https://github.com/jbbqqf/mlxtend.git fix/1167-minmax-constant-cols
git checkout FETCH_HEAD
pip install -e . --quiet
python /tmp/repro_1167.py
# Expected: column 0 is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], "has_nan = False", no warning
```

## What I ran locally

```text
$ pytest mlxtend/preprocessing/tests/test__scaling__minmax_scaling.py -v
============================== 6 passed in 0.60s ==============================

$ pytest mlxtend/preprocessing/ -v --timeout=60
============================== 41 passed in 0.80s ==============================
```

The three new regression tests fail on `origin/master`:
```
FAILED test__scaling__minmax_scaling.py::test_minmax_scaling_constant_column_numpy
  AssertionError: minmax_scaling produced NaN for a constant column; expected the column to be flattened to min_val (0.0).
FAILED test__scaling__minmax_scaling.py::test_minmax_scaling_constant_column_pandas
FAILED test__scaling__minmax_scaling.py::test_minmax_scaling_constant_column_custom_range
RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in divide
```

## Edge cases tested

| # | Scenario | Input | Expected | Verified by |
|---|----------|-------|----------|-------------|
| 1 | Constant column (numpy, default range) | `[[5,1],[5,2],[5,3]]` | column 0 → `0.0`, column 1 → `0/0.5/1` | `test_minmax_scaling_constant_column_numpy` |
| 2 | Constant column (pandas DataFrame) | `{"const":[5,5,5],"var":[1,2,3]}` | same, via `.loc` indexing path | `test_minmax_scaling_constant_column_pandas` |
| 3 | Constant column + custom `(min_val, max_val)` | `[[7,1],[7,2],[7,3]]`, `(50, 100)` | column 0 → `50.0` (the lower bound) | `test_minmax_scaling_constant_column_custom_range` |
| 4 | Non-constant columns (regression for existing behaviour) | original `test_pandas_minmax_scaling` / `test_numpy_minmax_scaling` inputs | unchanged | both pre-existing tests still pass |

## Risk / blast radius

Additive guard inside a single function. The new code path is only exercised when at least one selected column has zero range — previously that path produced NaN, now it produces `min_val`. Callers that relied on the NaN as a downstream sentinel will see a behavioural change, but that path was undocumented and inconsistent with `standardize`; the new behaviour matches the function's already-documented "rescaled column" contract.

## Release note

```release-note
minmax_scaling no longer returns silent NaNs for constant columns; constant columns are now collapsed to min_val, mirroring the existing contract of standardize (#1167).
```

### Description

`ExhaustiveFeatureSelector` evaluates every combination of features in `[min_features, max_features]`, which can produce a very large number of subsets. The recurring user complaint in #610 is that calling `get_metric_dict()` and turning the result into a DataFrame materialises *every* evaluated subset in memory.

pr_records.title: preprocessing: standardize constant columns to 0.0 (#1058)
pr_records.body:
### Code of Conduct

I have read the project's Code of Conduct.

### Description

`mlxtend.preprocessing.standardize` claims in its `Notes` section that
"if all values in a given column are the same, these values are all set
to `0.0`." For a constant column whose value is non-zero (e.g.
`[5, 5, 5]`), the function actually returns `[-5, -5, -5]` instead of
`[0, 0, 0]`. This PR brings the behaviour in line with the documented
contract.

The current code pre-zeroes the column and then runs
`(x - mean) / std`. With `std` forced to `1.0` and `mean` left untouched
at the original constant value, that yields `(0 - c) / 1 = -c` rather
than zero. Removing the pre-zero step lets the existing subtraction
collapse the column to exactly `0.0` (`(c - c) / 1.0 = 0`), which is the
intent.

The existing `test_zero_division_*` tests only ever used a constant
column of value `0`, so the bug never surfaced — `(0 - 0) / 1` is `0`
either way. The new regression tests here cover a non-zero constant
column.

Fixes #1058
